overview: Bahrain is a small island country in the Persian Gulf, linked to Saudi Arabia by a long causeway. Its capital and largest city is Manama. Bahrain became independent from British protection in 1971 and is a kingdom. Oil was found there in 1932, one of the first finds in the Gulf, and today banking and finance are also important.

geography.text: Bahrain is made up of a main island and dozens of smaller ones. The land is low and mostly desert, and parts of the coast have been extended with land reclaimed from the sea. Freshwater springs, both on land and under the sea, once made it an important stop for ships and pearl divers.

history.text: Bahrain was the centre of the ancient Dilmun civilisation, a trading hub between Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley. It was ruled by Portugal and Persia before the Al Khalifa family took control in 1783. Bahrain became a British protectorate in the 1800s, found oil in 1932, and became independent in 1971.

events.title: Causeway to Saudi Arabia
events.text: A 25-kilometre causeway links Bahrain to the mainland.

government.text: Bahrain is a constitutional monarchy ruled by the King from the Al Khalifa family, which holds most power. Parliament has an elected lower house and an upper house appointed by the King. Protests in 2011 were put down with help from Saudi troops.

economy.text: Bahrain was one of the first Gulf states to find oil, in 1932, but its reserves are smaller than its neighbours'. It has built up banking, aluminium and tourism. The King Fahd Causeway links it to Saudi Arabia.

culture.text: Bahrain was the centre of the ancient Dilmun civilisation. Pearl diving was its main industry for centuries, and a 'pearling trail' through Muharraq is a UNESCO site. The Qal'at al-Bahrain fort sits on a mound built up over 4,000 years.

items.title: Pearling Path
items.text: Houses and oyster beds of the pearl trade, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Qal'at al-Bahrain
items.text: A site settled for more than 4,000 years.

sport.text: The Bahrain Grand Prix, first held in 2004, was the first Formula 1 race in the Middle East. Football is the most popular sport to watch and play.

items.text: The first Formula 1 Grand Prix in the Middle East.

items.title: Gulf Cup
items.text: Bahrain won the football Gulf Cup in 2019 and 2024.
